lines.text: Two lines cross inside a triangle, right inside its circle. Exactly where do they cross?
lines.caption: Two lines cross inside a triangle, right inside its circle. Exactly where do they cross?

lines.text: A very tempting answer here is two to one. It's a trap, and you'll see why.
lines.caption: A very tempting answer here is two to one. It's a trap, and you'll see why.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's balance this triangle like a seesaw.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's balance this triangle like a seesaw.

lines.text: Triangle A B C has sides A B thirteen, B C fourteen, and C A fifteen.
lines.caption: Triangle ABC has sides AB thirteen, BC fourteen, and CA fifteen.

lines.text: The circle inside it touches B C at D, and C A at E. Segments A D and B E meet at P.
lines.caption: The circle inside it touches BC at D, and CA at E. Segments AD and BE meet at P.

lines.text: What is the ratio A P to P D? Here are the five choices.
lines.caption: What is the ratio AP to PD? Here are the five choices.

lines.text: So what are we really asked? How P splits A D into two parts, A P and P D.
lines.caption: So what are we really asked? How P splits AD into two parts, AP and PD.

lines.text: We know all three sides. First, we need to know exactly where D and E sit.
lines.caption: We know all three sides. First, we need to know exactly where D and E sit.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back!
lines.caption: Welcome back!

lines.text: From each corner, the two pieces out to the touch points have the same length.
lines.caption: From each corner, the two pieces out to the touch points have the same length.

lines.text: Here's the reason. Fold along the line from the corner to the circle's center. One piece lands on the other.
lines.caption: Here's the reason. Fold along the line from the corner to the circle's center. One piece lands on the other.

lines.text: Call the pieces x from A, y from B, and z from C.
lines.caption: Call the pieces x from A, y from B, and z from C.

lines.text: So x plus y is thirteen, y plus z is fourteen, z plus x is fifteen.
lines.caption: So x plus y is thirteen, y plus z is fourteen, z plus x is fifteen.

lines.text: Add all three sides: forty-two. Each letter shows up twice, so x plus y plus z is twenty-one.
lines.caption: Add all three sides: forty-two. Each letter shows up twice, so x plus y plus z is twenty-one.

lines.text: Take away B C, which is y plus z. That leaves x, twenty-one minus fourteen, which is seven.
lines.caption: Take away BC, which is y plus z. That leaves x, twenty-one minus fourteen, which is seven.

lines.text: In the same way, y is six, and z is eight.
lines.caption: In the same way, y is six, and z is eight.

lines.text: So B D is six and D C is eight. C E is eight and E A is seven.
lines.caption: So BD is six and DC is eight. CE is eight and EA is seven.

lines.text: Now for the fun part, mass points. Put a weight on each corner.
lines.caption: Now for the fun part, mass points. Put a weight on each corner.

lines.text: A seesaw balances when weight times distance is the same on both sides.
lines.caption: A seesaw balances when weight times distance is the same on both sides.

lines.text: For B C to balance at D, B's weight times six must equal C's weight times eight.
lines.caption: For BC to balance at D, B's weight times six must equal C's weight times eight.

lines.text: For C A to balance at E, C's weight times eight must equal A's weight times seven.
lines.caption: For CA to balance at E, C's weight times eight must equal A's weight times seven.

lines.text: So all three products match. Six, seven and eight all go into one hundred sixty-eight.
lines.caption: So all three products match. Six, seven and eight all go into one hundred sixty-eight.

lines.text: That makes B twenty-eight, C twenty-one, and A twenty-four.
lines.caption: That makes B twenty-eight, C twenty-one, and A twenty-four.

lines.text: Now merge B and C into one weight at D. Twenty-eight plus twenty-one is forty-nine.
lines.caption: Now merge B and C into one weight at D. Twenty-eight plus twenty-one is forty-nine.

lines.text: A and C merge at E, so it balances on B E too. Both lines meet at P: twenty-four at A, forty-nine at D.
lines.caption: A and C merge at E, so it balances on BE too. Both lines meet at P: twenty-four at A, forty-nine at D.

lines.text: Twenty-four times A P equals forty-nine times P D. So A P to P D is forty-nine to twenty-four.
lines.caption: Twenty-four times AP equals forty-nine times PD. So AP to PD is forty-nine to twenty-four.

lines.text: The answer is <short pause> forty-nine to twenty-four! Choice D.
lines.caption: The answer is forty-nine to twenty-four! Choice D.

lines.text: Here's a second way, with a parallel line.
lines.caption: Here's a second way, with a parallel line.

lines.text: Through D, draw a line parallel to B E. It hits side C A at a new point, G.
lines.caption: Through D, draw a line parallel to BE. It hits side CA at a new point, G.

lines.text: In triangle C B E, D G is parallel to B E. So G splits C E just like D splits C B: eight to six.
lines.caption: In triangle CBE, DG is parallel to BE. So G splits CE just like D splits CB: eight to six.

lines.text: That makes G E eight times six over fourteen, which is twenty-four over seven.
lines.caption: That makes GE eight times six over fourteen, which is twenty-four over seven.

lines.text: Now look at triangle A D G. P E is parallel to D G, so A P to P D equals A E to E G.
lines.caption: Now look at triangle ADG. PE is parallel to DG, so AP to PD equals AE to EG.

lines.text: That's seven divided by twenty-four over seven, which is forty-nine over twenty-four. Same answer!
lines.caption: That's seven divided by twenty-four over seven, which is forty-nine over twenty-four. Same answer!

lines.text: Pick this one when you'd rather not use weights.
lines.caption: Pick this one when you'd rather not use weights.

lines.text: Now, the traps.
lines.caption: Now, the traps.

lines.text: A, twenty-four to forty-nine, is P D to A P. It's our answer, flipped.
lines.caption: A, twenty-four to forty-nine, is PD to AP. It's our answer, flipped.

lines.text: B, seven to four, is what you'd get if G cut C E in half, making G E four.
lines.caption: B, seven to four, is what you'd get if G cut CE in half, making GE four.

lines.text: Choice C, two to one, is what you'd get using the tangent lengths as weights: fourteen at D, seven at A.
lines.caption: Choice C, two to one, is what you'd get using the tangent lengths as weights: fourteen at D, seven at A.

lines.text: But B C wouldn't balance. Six times six is thirty-six, but eight times eight is sixty-four.
lines.caption: But BC wouldn't balance. Six times six is thirty-six, but eight times eight is sixty-four.

lines.text: E, fifteen to seven, is what you'd get from C A to A E. That's a ratio on a side, not on A D.
lines.caption: E, fifteen to seven, is what you'd get from CA to AE. That's a ratio on a side, not on AD.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Check that every seesaw balances before you merge weights.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Check that every seesaw balances before you merge weights.

lines.text: Your turn! Same idea, new triangle. Now A B is three, B C is four, and C A is five.
lines.caption: Your turn! Same idea, new triangle. Now AB is three, BC is four, and CA is five.

lines.text: Same circle, same two lines. What is A P to P D?
lines.caption: Same circle, same two lines. What is AP to PD?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Tangent pieces first. Half the perimeter is six. So x is six minus four, which is two.
lines.caption: Tangent pieces first. Half the perimeter is six. So x is six minus four, which is two.

lines.text: In the same way, y is one, and z is three.
lines.caption: In the same way, y is one, and z is three.

lines.text: So B D is one, D C is three, C E is three, and E A is two.
lines.caption: So BD is one, DC is three, CE is three, and EA is two.

lines.text: The products must match: B times one, C times three, A times two. Make them all six.
lines.caption: The products must match: B times one, C times three, A times two. Make them all six.

lines.text: So B is six, C is two, and A is three. D gets six plus two, which is eight.
lines.caption: So B is six, C is two, and A is three. D gets six plus two, which is eight.

lines.text: So A P to P D is eight to three!
lines.caption: So AP to PD is eight to three!

lines.text: The big idea: equal tangents tell you exactly where the circle touches each side.
lines.caption: The big idea: equal tangents tell you exactly where the circle touches each side.

lines.text: Then weights that balance each side turn those pieces into the ratio along A D.
lines.caption: Then weights that balance each side turn those pieces into the ratio along AD.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
